During September 28, 2026 - October 5, 2026, we shipped 3 releases across 3 repositories (deploy frequency: 3 releases in 7 days).

This week's activity centered on the GitHub CI pipeline set: `ci-github-container` shipped 1 release and remained the busiest project (1 run), while `ci-github-publish` also shipped 1 release with the same 5-star footprint. The most recent release was `ci-github-nodejs` 0.25.0 on October 2, 2026, which indicates ongoing iteration in the Node.js CI path alongside the container build/publish flow, keeping the CI architecture consistent across language/runtime variants.

- `ci-github-container`: Continued focus on the container CI path matters for platform engineers because it is the highest-activity repo this period, which typically drives the most frequent feedback on build and packaging reliability.
- `ci-github-publish`: Publishing changes in this repo matter for SREs and release managers because it affects how artifacts are produced and made available, reducing friction when coordinating downstream deployments.
- `ci-github-nodejs` (0.25.0): The Node.js CI update matters for technical contributors because it improves the runtime-specific pipeline behavior they depend on, lowering the likelihood of environment-specific CI failures.

repositories.name: ci-github-container
repositories.description: Opinionated GitHub Actions and workflows for continuous integration in container (OCI) context

highlights:
## Release Summary

**Docker** adds image build-provenance attestations, pins the installed Docker version, updates BuildKit and Buildx, and supports pull-request image-tag cleanup for user-owned packages.

**Helm** adds a dedicated chart-signing action and configurable test namespaces, while fixing dependency vulnerabilities in documentation generation.

Internal maintenance refreshes dependencies, development tooling, and documentation, and fixes CI linting and Helm fixture security failures.

repositories.description: Opinionated Github actions and workflows for continuous integration in NodeJs context

highlights:
## Release Summary

Introduced `actions/publish` to publish CI-built npm packages directly from your own jobs, giving projects control over validation and GitHub release ordering. (https://github.com/hoverkraft-tech/ci-github-nodejs/pull/536)

Internal updates refresh dependencies and generated documentation, and streamline test-package maintenance and lint configuration. (https://github.com/hoverkraft-tech/ci-github-nodejs/pull/538)
